cards.front: Kernicterus is caused by the [___] fraction of bilirubin, which is lipid-soluble, poorly albumin-bound at high levels, and able to cross the neonatal blood-brain barrier.
cards.context:
This is the same fraction that rises in haemolysis (Rh/ABO, G6PD), which is why jaundice in the first 24 h is treated as a haemolytic emergency.

A raised conjugated (direct) fraction is a different problem — it does not cross the blood-brain barrier, is never physiological, and points to biliary atresia or neonatal hepatitis.

Trap: reading any neonatal jaundice as benign.

cards.front: In NSW, termination of pregnancy is available on request up to [___] weeks; beyond that requires two practitioners and a hospital setting.
cards.context:
The 22-week threshold in NSW (and most Australian states) reflects fetal viability and aligns with the legal framework when termination was decriminalised.

State-by-state variation: VIC allows on-request abortion to 24 weeks; QLD + SA cluster around 22 weeks.

 Since March 2024, WA allows abortion on request to 23 weeks; after 23 weeks two practitioners are required, and the former Ministerial Panel approval process has been abolished. Check current local legislation.

cards.front: Safer Baby Bundle: side-sleeping is recommended from [___] weeks because supine sleep doubles late stillbirth risk via IVC compression.
cards.context: The supine-sleep effect is mechanical — the gravid uterus compresses the IVC, halving venous return and dropping cardiac output enough to reduce uteroplacental perfusion.

cards.front: The 4 Ts of postpartum haemorrhage are Tone (commonest, ~70%), Trauma (lacerations), [___] (retained), and Thrombin (coagulopathy).
cards.context:
The 4 Ts mnemonic for PPH ranks causes by frequency: Tone (atony, ~70%), Trauma (~20%), Tissue (~10%), Thrombin (<1%).

Trauma — cervical/vaginal/perineal lacerations, uterine rupture → surgical repair; Tissue — retained placenta/membranes → manual removal; Thrombin — coagulopathy (DIC, anticoagulants) → correct with blood products.

cards.front: In suspected ovarian torsion, a normal colour Doppler does NOT exclude the diagnosis; proceed to [___] if clinical suspicion is high.
cards.context:
The Doppler trap in ovarian torsion is intermittent flow.

Time to detorsion drives ovarian salvage rates. Detorsion within 6-8 hours of symptom onset usually preserves the ovary; beyond 24 hours, necrosis is likely.

So when the clinical picture is right (sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain, peritonism, vomiting, adnexal mass on imaging) — go straight to laparoscopy.

cards.front: Small for gestational age (SGA) = estimated fetal weight (EFW) <[___]th centile; fetal growth restriction (FGR) is pathological, usually <3rd centile or abnormal Dopplers.
cards.context:
The trap: SGA is a size label, FGR is a diagnosis of failed growth potential.

SGA just means EFW <10th centile. Many are constitutionally small but healthy (small parents, female fetus), needing only surveillance to confirm normal velocity with normal Dopplers.

FGR is the pathological subset, flagged by centile <3rd OR abnormal umbilical artery Dopplers signalling placental insufficiency. Doppler separates the at-risk fetus from the merely small one and drives delivery.

cards.front: [___] manoeuvre dislocates a located hip (push posteriorly); Ortolani manoeuvre reduces a dislocated hip (lift anteriorly). Both lose reliability after 3 months.
cards.context:
The two manoeuvres test opposites. Barlow (push posteriorly) tests if a LOCATED hip can be dislocated — flex, adduct, push posteriorly; positive if 'clunk' as head dislocates.

Ortolani (pull anteriorly) tests if a DISLOCATED hip can be reduced — flex, abduct, lift greater trochanter forward; positive if clunk indicates reduction.

Mnemonic: Barlow Backward, Ortolani Out. Both become unreliable after 3 months as the hip stabilises in dislocation — replaced by Galeazzi sign, limited abduction, asymmetric thigh creases.

cards.front: The single biggest risk factor for postpartum endometritis is route of birth: caesarean section; treatment is amoxicillin + gentamicin + [___].
cards.context:
Endometritis is polymicrobial bacterial infection of the endometrium + adjacent decidua.

Presentation: fever ≥38°C, lower abdominal/uterine tenderness, malodorous lochia, raised WCC.

Consider differentials (wound infection, retained products, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis).

cards.front: Shoulder dystocia mnemonic HELPERR — Help, Evaluate episiotomy, [___] (McRoberts), Pressure (suprapubic, NEVER fundal), Enter, Remove posterior arm, Roll.
cards.context:
HELPERR enforces an order to prevent chaotic responses that cost babies their brachial plexus.

H = Help (call obstetric, anaesthetic, paediatric help, document times); E = Evaluate for episiotomy; L = Legs to McRoberts (first-line, resolves 60-90% with suprapubic pressure); P = suprapubic Pressure.

cards.front: Causes of oligohydramnios include PROM, fetal renal agenesis (Potter sequence), uteroplacental insufficiency, and [___] pregnancy.
cards.context:
Fetal urine is the dominant source of amniotic fluid from T2 onwards — anything reducing fetal urine production or allowing fluid escape produces oligohydramnios.

Causes: PROM (fluid escape); renal agenesis (Potter sequence — no source); uteroplacental insufficiency (reduced renal perfusion); post-dates (placental decline).

cards.front: Pregnancy obesity is BMI ≥30 kg/m²; risk of gestational diabetes (GDM) rises 3-5-fold and risk of stillbirth rises [___]-fold.
cards.context:
Obesity (BMI ≥30) is the single largest modifiable risk factor in modern obstetrics.

Risks rise across the board: GDM (3-5×), hypertensive disease (2-3×), VTE (2-4×), failed induction/C-section (2×), and PPH from the over-distended uterus.

The stillbirth signal is why obesity is built into late-pregnancy surveillance — and poorer ultrasound views mean anomalies like NTDs are more easily missed.

cards.front: In pregnancy, plasma volume rises more than red cell mass, causing a physiological (dilutional) [___].
cards.context: Plasma volume rises proportionally more than red cell mass, so the haemoglobin concentration falls even though red cell mass increases — a dilutional effect, not true iron deficiency (though that can coexist).

cards.front: In healthy term infants, cord clamping is typically delayed for at least 60 seconds; this increases neonatal [___] stores and reduces anaemia at 4-6 months.
cards.context:
Delayed cord clamping (≥60 sec, often 1-3 min) allows ~80-100 mL of placental-to-neonatal transfusion — boosting blood volume ~25%, raising iron stores, reducing anaemia at 4-6 months.

Cochrane backs it as standard for healthy term and preterm babies; the old 'clamp and cut immediately' is now wrong.

Immediate clamping is still preferred for severe maternal haemorrhage or when the neonate needs immediate resuscitation (unless 'resuscitation with cord intact' is possible).

cards.front: The model of antenatal care is determined by [___] at the booking visit; high-risk women need obstetrician-led care.
cards.context:
Risk assessment at booking sorts women into pathways: low-risk women choose between shared care (GP + obstetrician), midwifery group practice (continuity-of-carer with documented reductions in interventions).

Triggers for high-risk pathway: pre-existing HTN, diabetes, autoimmune disease, cardiac disease, BMI >40, prior HDP/stillbirth/preterm birth, multiple pregnancy, significant mental health conditions.

cards.front: Trial of labour after caesarean: baseline uterine rupture risk is approximately 0.5% in experienced centres; risk [___] with oxytocin augmentation. Overall TOLAC success rate is around 70%.
cards.context:
VBAC carries a small but real risk of uterine rupture along the previous scar — ~1:200 (0.5%) in experienced centres for a single previous transverse lower segment CS.

Risk doubles with oxytocin augmentation (over-stimulation stresses scar), rises with prior classical (vertical) incision (~5-10% — generally contraindicates VBAC), multiple previous CS.

VBAC success rate ~70%, lower without prior vaginal birth + recurrent CS indication.

cards.front: Baby blues is common (~70-80%), peaks at days [___], and is self-limiting; symptoms persisting beyond 2 weeks need postnatal depression screening with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS).
cards.context:
Baby blues vs PND is told apart by timing and trajectory. Baby blues is a transient mood lability peaking days 3-5 (the oestrogen/progesterone crash) that settles by 2 weeks — reassurance, not treatment.

The 2-week mark is the trigger to act: mood symptoms still present beyond it are no longer normal and need EPDS screening for PND.

PND affects 10-17% and is often missed because its peak (3-6 months) falls after the antenatal team has handed over.

cards.front: A perineal tear involving the anal sphincter complex is a third- or [___]-degree tear.
cards.context: The grading hinges on the anal sphincter. 1st = skin/mucosa, 2nd = perineal muscle, 3rd = anal sphincter involved, 4th = through to rectal mucosa. 3rd/4th (OASIS) need theatre repair and carry incontinence risk.

cards.front: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk peaks in the first 6 weeks postpartum, with [___]'s triad (endothelial damage, stasis, hypercoagulability) all firing.
cards.context:
Pregnancy is prothrombotic throughout, but the 6-week postpartum window is peak VTE risk — 20-80× non-pregnant baseline.

VTE prophylaxis assessment mandatory at every postpartum encounter (delivery, discharge, postnatal review).
